title: Antihistamines | NHS inform
text:
Antihistamines
Antihistamines are used to treat symptoms of
allergies
.
They’re also sometimes used to treat:
motion sickness
feeling sick (nausea) or
being sick (vomiting)
insomnia
Most antihistamines can be bought from local
pharmacies
and shops. Some are only available on prescription.
How antihistamines work
Antihistamines work by blocking the effects of a substance called histamine in your body.
Histamine is usually released when your body detects something harmful, like an infection. It causes blood vessels to expand and the skin to swell. This helps protect the body.
If you have allergies, the body mistakes something harmless like pollen, pet hair or house dust as being harmful. This causes the body to produce histamine.
Histamine causes an allergic reaction with symptoms, including:
itchy and watery eyes
a running or
blocked nose
sneezing
skin rashes
Antihistamine medication helps to stop this from happening if you take it before coming into contact with a substance you’re allergic to. Antihistamines can also reduce the severity of your symptoms if you take them afterwards.
Types of antihistamines
There are different types of antihistamines, including:
antihistamines that make you feel drowsy (sleepy) – like chlorphenamine (Piriton), cinnarizine, diphenydramine, hydroxyzine and promethazine
non-drowsy antihistamines that are less likely to make you feel sleepy – like acrivastine, cetirizine, fexofenadine and loratadine
Antihistamines come in different forms, including:
tablets
capsules
liquids
syrups
creams
lotions
gels
eyedrops
nasal sprays
Some people find that certain types of antihistamines work better for them than others. Ask a pharmacist or healthcare professional for advice if you’re unsure about what medicine is best for you.
Some types of antihistamines may be available on
NHS Pharmacy First Scotland
. Speak to your local pharmacist for more information.
Find your nearest pharmacy
How to take antihistamines
Your healthcare professional or pharmacist will tell you how to take your antihistamine. You should follow the directions on the label. Read the patient information leaflet that comes with your medicine too. If you have any questions about taking an antihistamine, ask your pharmacist for advice.
Possible side effects
Antihistamines can have side effects. These side effects are usually mild and should pass once you finish your course of treatment.
Antihistamines that make you drowsy
Side effects of antihistamines that make you drowsy can include:
sleepiness (drowsiness) – do not drive or use machinery after taking these antihistamines
dry mouth
blurred vision
difficulty peeing
Side effects of non-drowsy antihistamines can include:
headache
dry mouth
feeling sick
drowsiness – this is less common with non-drowsy antihistamines but it can still happen
You should check the patient leaflet that comes with your medicine for a full list of possible side effects.
Reporting side effects
The Yellow Card Scheme allows you to report suspected side effects from any medicine you’re taking. It’s run by a medicines safety watchdog called the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA).
Further information on the Yellow Card Scheme
Warnings and precautions
Some antihistamines can interact with:
antidepressants
stomach ulcer
or indigestion medicines
cold and flu remedies that also contain an antihistamine
Alcohol can increase the chance that antihistamines will make you feel drowsy. You should try not to drink alcohol while taking antihistamines.
Food and other drinks do not affect most antihistamines. However, you should check the patient leaflet that comes with your medicine to make sure.
Who can take antihistamines?
Most people can take antihistamines.
Some antihistamines may not be suitable if you:
are pregnant or breastfeeding
are looking for a medicine for a young child
are an older person
are taking other medicines
have an underlying health condition, like
heart disease
,
liver disease
,
kidney disease
or
epilepsy
Ask your healthcare professional or pharmacist for advice before taking this medication. You should also let them know if you’re taking other prescribed medicines.
